My friend and I starting lifting. We have an easy to follow program 2 day split with a list of various exercises. We often skip an exercise if the equipment we need is being used, move on to the next, and jump back once the equipment opens up. The gym was stupid busy the other day, and oddly enough we ended up doing out list backwards. The exercises that we normally do first were now last, and both of us couldn't do our normal weight or reps.

 

More info: typically, we do bench and chest work, then back & lat work. This day we started with back and the back numbers were better but the chest work was more degrees worse than the back improvement. Also, I hate doing squats last, for the same reason. Less weight, less reps.

 

I find this interesting and was wondering if other people work with this and switch for better overall numbers, or do you stick to a certain order?
Observation: order of exercises and the improved/reduced results

Generally, you're going to want to stick to a definite order. You experienced what happens when you change. It's helpful to be consistent, so your results can be measured as accurately as possible.

When it comes to exercises, I like to start with larger compound movements (squat, bench, etc) and then go to isolation exercises (bicep curl). But it is all relative to what works best for you.

We generally do try to stick to the same order, but when the gym is packed we sometimes end up skipping one because the equipment is is use. Side note: I love the paradox that a busy gym is great for business, but most people like an empty gym :)

I know exactly what you are talking about. It's kinda weird: If no one joins, the gym closes down. But if a lot of people show up, then no one can use the gym. There is definitely a sweet spot for the amount of people a gym can operate effectively at.

For just general physical fitness, it's not vital to maintain an order if you're trying to balance use of your time. It's a good practice to get into, and is definitely necessary if your goals change and you want to get into competing in strength sports. But since you and your friend are just starting out, just getting in the gym and getting better will yield results.

Sorry for the novel, I'll try to answer any questions you have.
Thx. Right now, I'm enjoying how everything feels like an experiment. Noting my observations, and learning by trial and error. I don't think competing will ever come into it, but never say never. :)

That's the correct approach to have when starting out. It's very easy to get locked into an ideology of lifting, which will limit progress. Lots of people have gotten very strong by trial and error. Good luck!
